reciprocal_reviewers.description: Reciprocal Reviewer for your submission will be assigned three other submissions to review in exchange for your own reviews. Nominated reviewers must be listed as authors of this submission and must complete their assigned reviews on time. As the Authors rely on the timeliness of the reviews with registration slots, **submissions that do not meet this requirement, or whose nominated reviewers fail to submit their reviews, will be desk rejected and not considered for awards.** Search by name or profile ID for the authors of this submission.

param.mismatchError: must be a valid OpenReview profile ID starting with ~.

voluntary_reviewers.description: Voluntary Reviewers will be assigned three or fewer submissions to review. **Both Reciprical and Voluntary Reviewers will be considered for Outstanding Reviewer awards, warranting an extra full conference registration slot at NeurIPS 2026 in Paris.** Please note that we rely on the timeliness of Voluntary Reviewers, and so the same conditions apply to Voluntary Reviewers as the Reciprocal Reviewers.

param.mismatchError: must be a valid OpenReview profile ID starting with ~.

white_box_award.description: Tick this box if your submission should be considered for the White-Box Award. Your method's verdict must depend on signals beyond the generated text (e.g. activations, probes, SAEs, patching, steering), and your report must include an ablation with vs. without the white-box component. Please note that token-level logprobs alone are not sufficient to be considered for the white-box award.

ai_assistance.description: AI assistance disclosure. Tick every area in which generative AI tools (e.g. LLM chat assistants, coding assistants, agents) were used. If no AI assistance was used, tick only the last option. Your answers here must match the AI Use Statement in your paper.

items.description: Ideation: proposing or refining hypotheses, developing theoretical models or conceptual frameworks, formulating mathematical claims or proofs, designing methodology or experiments, brainstorming topics, literature search and summarization
Coding: implementing methods, creating or editing code, suggesting experimental parameters, generating synthetic data, cleaning or reformatting datasets
Analysis: interpreting results, supporting qualitative or thematic analysis, creating or modifying figures
Writing: drafting parts of the paper, translation, editing for readability, suggesting structure, title or keywords, formatting references

ai_use_statement.description: Every paper must include a mandatory 'AI Use Statement' section after the main text and before the references. It does not count toward the page limit. The statement must (1) name the tasks for which generative AI tools were used and which tools, (2) name the relevant tasks for which they were not used, and (3) confirm that the authors reviewed all AI-assisted work and take full responsibility for the final content, including AI-assisted text, claims, code, and other artifacts. Suggested structure: 'In this work, we used generative AI tools for <tasks>. We did not use generative AI tools for <other tasks>. We have reviewed all AI-assisted work and take responsibility for the final content of this paper.' More detail is welcome. If no AI assistance was used, the statement must say so. Missing statements, or falsehoods, plagiarism or misrepresentation introduced through AI tools, are treated as violations of the Code of Ethics and may lead to desk rejection.

enum: We confirm that our paper includes an AI Use Statement consistent with the boxes ticked above, and that we take full responsibility for all AI-assisted content.
